prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, from bifunctional PROTAC degraders to the cereblon-dependent mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a clean chemical idea, using a designed small molecule to bring a chosen protein to an E3 ligase so that the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery destroys it. Four of eight opening ballots put B023 first and five placed it in the top three, and I rank it first on the science, not on that count. It rests on real molecular design (linker and ternary-complex chemistry, ligase ligands, cooperativity). It has opened targets that occupancy-based inhibitors could not reach, and the mechanism has been reproduced by many independent groups. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains how glue degraders work and ties both strands to the same ubiquitin-ligase logic. That gives a coherent single achievement, induced proximity for degradation, within a three-person limit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that no bifunctional degrader has yet been approved as a drug, so part of the case is forward-looking. Somfai and Zou both flag this, and the clinical pipeline could still disappoint. A second problem is attribution. Ciulli's VHL ligands and structure-guided ternary-complex work, Gray's degrader chemistry, and Sakamoto, Ito and Kim are all left out of any three-person set. Whoever is omitted, the prize will look arbitrary to part of the field. Finally, PROTACs and glues may really be two discoveries with different histories, in which case one citation joins them somewhat artificially.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B023 first but prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that Ciulli's VHL ligand and ternary-complex structural work turned PROTACs into a general, drug-like platform, and that the Handa/Ito and Gray strands are unresolved alternatives.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli argument seriously; the structure-guided turn from peptidic to drug-like degraders is real chemistry, and I would not call it secondary. I still keep Handa as the third name. The cereblon mechanism explains how a whole class of glue degraders acts, including thalidomide-type drugs that are already in patients. It is also the more clearly independent discovery, whereas Ciulli's work builds on the Crews/Deshaies concept. If the committee prefers Ciulli, I could accept that, but then the citation must be worded narrowly around PROTACs and should not claim the glue mechanism.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling first, calling it a mature, ubiquitous synthetic method with a clean two-person attribution, and ranks protein degradation only eighth because clinical validation is still emerging.
responses.response: The attribution for B002 is cleaner than for any other shortlisted candidate, and I accept that B002 is fully mature. My disagreement is about originality and timing. It follows the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize, which narrows how new the recognition would feel. I also read the lack of an approved PROTAC as less of a problem than Somfai does. The Nobel standard is a validated, reproducible chemical principle, and degraders have that. Both arguments are legitimate, so I name B002 as an alternative and do not dismiss it.

responses.point: Sparr ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first, as a physical-chemistry achievement in lipid self-assembly that made siRNA and mRNA medicines practical. She argues that the 2023 Medicine prize left the delivery side unrecognized.
responses.response: I agree the impact is exceptional, and the lipid self-assembly framing is convincing. I ranked B041 sixth because I find the attribution much harder to settle than for B023. The credit spreads over Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and it is entangled with patent and company histories. The overlap with the 2023 mRNA prize also still seems to me to weigh on how the committee would present it. I would not object to B041 later, but I cannot yet identify a three-name set that I think is defensible.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks proton-coupled electron transfer (B028) first as a mature, unifying physical-chemical concept spanning enzymes and electrocatalysis, with Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer and Nocera making complementary contributions.
responses.response: B028 is mature and conceptually broad, and I did not rank it, which in hindsight may undervalue it. My hesitation is that the concept is spread over biology, theory and catalysis, so a single citation will be diffuse. Meyer's early role also makes a three-person cut harder than it first appears. It does not change my first choice, but a colleague who knows the enzymology better than I do could tell me whether that diffuseness is real.

uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be treated as one discovery or two, and whether a single citation can honestly cover both.
Whether the committee will accept Handa or prefer Ciulli as the third laureate, which decides whether the glue mechanism is credited.
Current clinical status of degraders; I have not verified whether any approval has occurred.
Whether condensate biology (B021) will be judged mature enough in a later round.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B023, B021 or B002. My work on peptides, nanoparticle biosensing and biomaterials at Linkoping is adjacent to but does not overlap with these candidates. I have no documented connection to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Buchwald or Hartwig. My postdoc mentors were Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey, neither of whom is a shortlisted name.
